name: Laetiporus sulphureus

tip_speed.source: Dzyhun 2020, Biology of basidiomycete macromycetes Laetiporus sulphureus and Cerioporus squamosus in culture, PhD thesis abstract, M.G. Kholodny Institute of Botany, National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
tip_speed.note: radial growth of 13 strains on agar media ranged from 5.2 to 10.4 mm/day; midpoint 7.8 mm/day x 41.7. Read from the thesis abstract only: the temperature and medium for each figure are not stated there (28 C was the best temperature, beer wort agar the best medium). Luangharn et al. 2014 (Mycology 5:221-227) report 11.5 to 12.2 mm/day at 25 C for two Thai strains of L. sulphureus sensu lato, but their rate calculation is unclear

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Dzyhun 2020, Biology of basidiomycete macromycetes Laetiporus sulphureus and Cerioporus squamosus in culture, PhD thesis abstract, M.G. Kholodny Institute of Botany, National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
t_opt.note: best of the temperatures tested, 13 strains (thesis abstract). Luangharn et al. 2014 found two Thai strains fastest at 25 C on malt extract agar

t_max.source: Dzyhun 2020, Biology of basidiomycete macromycetes Laetiporus sulphureus and Cerioporus squamosus in culture, PhD thesis abstract, M.G. Kholodny Institute of Botany, National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
t_max.note: stated upper limit for the strains (thesis abstract). The two Thai strains of Luangharn et al. 2014 did not grow at 35 C

cold_drop.note: Pleszczynska et al. 2013 (World J. Microbiol. Biotechnol. 29:753-758, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3599174) grew the mycelium at 23 C and got fruiting only after a cold shock: 10 C water injected into the bag (used here, 23 - 10 = 13), or 24 h at 2 to 4 C, which worked less well. A brief shock, not a sustained drop; fruit bodies then formed at 23 C

ecology.substrate: heartwood of living oak and other trees

size_cm.source: First Nature (P. O'Reilly), Laetiporus sulphureus, Chicken-of-the-Woods, species page
size_cm.note: width of one bracket; 3 to 12 cm thick. Tiers of brackets are larger. Field-guide web page

notes: Parasite and saprotroph: a heart rot in the standing trunk that hollows trees. The survey codes it MAT/HOST.
